verdict.reasoning: The patient reports left-sided hearing difficulty for six weeks: 'For about six weeks' and later clarifies it is 'Just the left ear, yeah.'
Intermittent nature is stated: Doctor asks if symptoms have been on and off, and patient replies, 'It's kind of on and off.' This refers to the six-week period.
Patient describes a similar brief episode about a year ago: 'I had something maybe about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days.'

Patient describes intermittent left-sided tinnitus triggered by TV or music: 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear... it's kind of on and off... if I'm watching TV or listening to music or something. Something that will set off the ringing in the ear.'

Patient reports mild episodic dizziness and feeling off-balance: 'there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well' and later clarifies 'just a little bit kind of off balance.'

Patient links feeling sick with dizziness: 'there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well,' and the doctor asks about 'dizziness that you've been getting,' indicating association. This supports occasional nausea with dizziness.

Patient denies true vertigo: 'It's not that kind of dizziness you get with nausea, like not proper room spinning or anything like that, but just a little bit kind of off balance,' which indicates no true spinning vertigo.
Right ear appears normal per patient: Doctor asks, 'So your right ear is fine?' and patient replies, 'It seems to be, yeah.'

Fever is denied: Doctor asks, 'Have you been experiencing any fever?' Patient responds, 'Not specifically, apart from the dizziness and sickness I mentioned before,' which serves as a denial of fever.
Chest pain is denied: Doctor asks, 'Have you any chest pain with it?' and patient responds, 'No.'
Ear itching is denied: Doctor asks, 'And has your ear been itchy at all?' Patient replies, 'No.'
No cotton bud use is reported: Doctor asks, 'do you use cotton wool buds to try and clean out wax from your ears?' Patient replies, 'No.'

The note summarizes: left-sided hearing loss for six weeks ('For about six weeks' and 'Just the left ear, yeah'), intermittent tinnitus and disequilibrium ('ringing in my left ear... on and off' and 'a bit dizzy... off balance'), and doctor states need to rule out wax blockage: 'Simple things might be wax... impacted wax blocking the tube... we need to exclude that first.'

Doctor indicates that if no external obstruction, inner structures are considered: 'If that's the case [wax]... we need to exclude that first and then after that we can consider other potential possibilities... It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear.'
Intermittent left-sided tinnitus is described: 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear... it's kind of on and off.'

Tinnitus education is initiated: Doctor explains tinnitus and its nature and says, 'I'm going to paste the link for a leaflet about tinnitus in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it.'

Face-to-face appointment in 4–5 days for ear examination is planned: 'book you in for a face to face appointment in one of our clinics... within the next four, five days or so... one of the GP will just have a quick look down the ear, figure out whether there's a physical blockage or whether there's something else going on.' This implies otoscopy of canal/tympanic membrane and assessment for wax vs other pathology.

Though not phrased as a treatment step, the plan is to deal with wax if present and consider other causes if normal: 'Someone might have impacted wax... which can lead to muffled hearing. If that's the case, that that's something that's easily fixable... we need to exclude that first and then after that we can consider other potential possibilities.'
A tinnitus leaflet will be provided: 'I'm going to paste the link for a leaflet about tinnitus in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it.'

Admin staff will schedule and patient is to call: 'I'll send a message to our admin team, I'll ask them to slot you into one of our clinics... I'll leave the number in the notes of this appointment, ring them, and then they'll slot you in.'

Patient advised to seek care sooner if issues arise: 'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to her and we'll serve a video.' This implies return sooner if symptoms worsen or problems occur.
Follow-up face-to-face otoscopy in 4–5 days: 'book you in for a face to face appointment... within the next four, five days or so.'
Instruction to return if problems before scheduled visit: 'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment.'
